rulings.currentText: `Ω_B1..Ω_B6` for the per-relay bias resistor, `Ω_220` for a plain 220 Ω part, bare `Ω` for the optional motor-speed resistor.
rulings.ruling: correct and widen. Replace with: a numeric subscript denotes a plain resistor of that value in ohms — `Ω_220` (Book VII p.11, 220 Ω between `1cap` and `1+`) and `Ω_22` (22 Ω, used repeatedly in the automatic-counter programs on printed pp.20–21); `Ω_B1..Ω_B6` is the per-relay bias resistor; a **bare `Ω` means a resistor whose value is not yet fixed** — used for the trial resistor in the bias-selection procedure `(+/Ω)(Ω/E)` on printed p.8 as well as for the optional motor-speed resistor `(D18/Ω)(Ω/D19)` on printed p.21. rulings.evidence: maintenance-manual.pdf PDF p-05 (printed 3) rendered at 700 dpi and cropped: the rectifier-output node marked '+' runs right to the + terminal blob; the transformer centre tap runs through a switch symbol labelled CIRCUIT BREAKER to the − terminal blob; a lamp symbol labelled POWER LIGHT bridges the + and − rails downstream of the breaker. No fuse symbol appears. Parts list (printed p.11): 6431 Circuit Breaker, 6432 Slide Switch, 6433 Rectifier, 6434 Transformer, 6435 Light Assembly, 6436 Pushbutton Switch, 6437 Relay, 6471 Motor, 6472 Drive Wheel, 6473 Rotary Switch Assembly, 6490/6491 wires.

rulings.currentText: | Power supply | 1 | PLUS rail, MINUS rail | 110 V AC → nominal 12 V DC, ~13 V unloaded, 1.5 A continuous; resettable circuit breaker in series; ON/OFF switch; indicator lamp. None of these four controls has a jack. | [verified] | Book I p.3; Maint. pp.2–3 |
rulings.ruling: add what the schematic actually shows, since this file is the netlist spec and the Maintenance Manual is the only source that draws the supply. Extend the topology cell to: '110 V AC → transformer with centre-tapped secondary → two-diode full-wave rectifier; the diode junction is the PLUS node, the centre tap is the MINUS node. Nominal 12 V DC, ~13 V unloaded, 1.5 A continuous. The resettable circuit breaker sits in series in the **minus** leg (the centre-tap lead), so a trip opens the minus rail and every load with it. The indicator lamp is wired permanently across + and − downstream of the breaker — the rails are never truly unloaded. **No smoothing capacitor is drawn**, so what the figure depicts is unfiltered full-wave rectified DC; treat ripple as an electrical-model question, not a netlist one, and cross-reference the electrical-model file rather than asserting a filtered rail here. None of the four controls has a jack.'
rulings.evidence: maintenance-manual.pdf PDF p-05 (printed 3), Power Supply Circuit Diagram, read at 700 dpi. Corroborated by the manual's own step 9 (printed p.4): 'Connect a binary output light between the + power supply terminal and the circuit breaker terminal which leads to the transformer ... between the + power supply terminal and the circuit breaker terminal which leads to the power light' — both breaker terminals are referenced against +, i.e. the breaker is not in the + leg. Step 12: 'if there is not proper DC output between the transformer center top (yellow lead) and the center terminal on the rectifier, the rectifier is defective'.

rulings.section: 1, designator grammar table — after the 'Matrix junction' row, or as a new paragraph beside the 'no `Q` terminal' note

rulings.section: 7, 'Isolation.' paragraph (and the matching note in §9 under Relay Check)
rulings.currentText: **Isolation.** The two contact sets of one relay are electrically isolated: `nH` and `nL` are distinct nodes, and `nG`/`nJ`/`nK`/`nN` are four further distinct nodes. No source says so in words; it is a deduction from two published programs whose printed results are impossible under a common arm.
rulings.ruling: split the claim by what each source actually carries, so a later pass neither over-credits nor re-opens the Relay Check figure. Rewrite as: 'The two contact sets of one relay are electrically isolated. Two separate claims, on different evidence. (a) `nG`, `nJ`, `nK`, `nN` are four distinct nodes: the Maintenance Manual Relay Check figure (printed p.7) drives four different lamps from them and prints results that distinguish `{J,N}` from `{G,K}`; Book I p.12 additionally calls H–J and L–N *"separate electrical connections"*. (b) `nH` and `nL` are distinct nodes: **no source says so in words, and the Relay Check does not settle it** — that figure feeds both arms from `+`, so a common arm would be observationally identical there. It is a deduction from two published programs whose printed results are impossible under a common arm (§9). What the figure does contribute is that SDC spends two wires, `+/H` and `+/L`, where one would do.' Also strengthen §9's Relay Check note from 'One would do if the arms were common' to 'One would do if the arms were common — suggestive, not proof; the proof is Book II Experiments 5 and 6.'
rulings.evidence: maintenance-manual.pdf PDF p-09 (printed 7), Relay Check figure traced at 600 dpi. Netlist read off the figure: `+/H`, `+/L`, `+/Y`, `X/E`, `F/-`, `J/1A`, `1B/1-`, `G/2A`, `2B/2-`, `N/3A`, `3B/3-`, `K/4A`, `4B/4-`; C is drawn as a dangling terminal, the coil sits in its own E–F loop, and a dashed vertical runs from the coil through both contact sets. Under H≡L the printed result 'Lights 1 and 3 on, then 2 and 4' is unchanged, so the figure cannot discriminate.
